verdict.rationale: Bitwarden documents its own programmatic vault surfaces: a CLI described as 'fully-featured' for 'accessing and managing your vault', a `bw serve` local REST Vault Management API, personal API keys for automated workflows, and an official MCP server that completed a live handshake. However, the evidence only shows querying TOTP codes and items; it never explicitly documents creating or editing items or seeding TOTP secrets programmatically. missing for 10: explicit documentation of item create/edit operations via CLI/REST/MCP, programmatic TOTP-secret seeding, evidence of which MCP tools are write-capable, hands-on corroboration of agent-driven writes

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can create and update vault entries — seeding new TOTP secrets, storing credentials — through documented programmatic surfaces

citations.quote: The Bitwarden command-line interface (CLI) is a powerful, fully-featured tool for accessing and managing your vault.
exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API)
Using the personal API key for CLI authentication is suitable for automated workflows
Bitwarden's OFFICIAL MCP server completed a FULL keyless stdio initialize handshake
